text:
Sam: heads-up — multiple hosted-api customers in eu-west-1 reporting a sharp uptick in 502/504s for streaming /v1/generate calls starting ~09:12 UTC. error rate ~8% for streaming shards, normal for non-streaming. sample trace id: trace-0a1b2c3d.
Leah: on it. looking at edge envoy clusters — upstream resets and stream-abort spikes. envoy log snippet: `level=error msg=UpstreamReset: stream id=245 upstream_reset_reason=UPSTREAM_REMOTE_RESET` — repeats for same cluster.
Priya: I'm seeing a correlated jump in large header frames from several tenants around the same window. HPACK header table growth looks suspicious (lots of long model-meta headers).
Nate: can anyone repro with a curl sample? sending long metadata headers over http2 often surfaces HPACK issues.
Sam: repro steps sent by customer (condensed):
```
curl -v --http2 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "X-Model-Meta: $(python -c 'print("a"*2500)')" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?stream=true"
```
Response: connection reset after ~5s, 502 from edge.
Leah: traced the request through our frontdoor -> envoys -> midproxy pool. midproxy reports `stream window exceeded` logs followed by `connection closed by upstream`. looks like header compression state thrashing when large, infrequent header values are introduced to the HPACK dynamic table.
Priya: we recently rotated midproxy instances for a minor config push in eu-west-1 at 09:10. hypothesize: when new midproxy nodes join they advertise fresh HPACK state and some envoy-to-envoy streams get reset while dynamic tables resync, causing transient 5xx for streaming calls that rely on persistent stream state.
Nate: quick mitigation options: 1) add a temporary routing rule to steer streaming traffic to the streaming-optimized pool that has HPACK disabled (edge-route: streaming-opt). 2) bump upstream connection drain time to let existing streams finish during scaling. 3) short-term: advise customers to avoid huge model-meta headers (<=512 chars) until we patch.
Leah: I can apply routing rule now as a canary for eu-west-1. will also enable verbose envoy hpack logging for 10m.
deploy-bot: canary route `streaming-opt` created in eu-west-1 by Leah at 09:24 UTC (id: canary-1934567800-1).
Maya: @customers — pinging affected accounts with suggested workaround (use route header `X-Edge-Route: streaming-opt` or trim large headers). will update ticket with trace id and ETA.
Sam: follow-up for eng-runtime: can we reproduce locally with multiple envoy instances and churn? Nate/Nate-team to spin up test harness.
Nate: yes, will reproduce using two envoys + midproxy and churn node join/leave while streaming long headers. I’ll capture pcap and envoy admin stats (hpack table size, stream resets).
Priya: longer-term fix: patch midproxy scaling flow to warm HPACK state or disable dynamic table advertising for streaming routes; eng-sre + eng-runtime to propose PR.
Leah: current status: canary route holding ~90% of streaming traffic and error rate in eu-west-1 dropped from 8% -> 0.6% in last 6m. keeping monitoring for 30m then schedule controlled rollout.
Maya: customer comms drafted, will send once we confirm stable for 30m.
Sam: thanks all — saving logs and traces to the ticket. next update in 20m or on significant change. :thumbsup:
